doc.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002

title: Joining the union at seventeen, first bands
summary: Alley and Saunders King bands, a teen band in the barber's basement, James Brown's band; he joins the subsidiary union for five dollars down.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: on the radio with a singing group and he had a bit of a name, so they got Saunders to front the band. And so anyhow I’d go by and watch the rehearsals and I’d watch the drummer, Maxey, Norville Maxey was the drummer. I’d watch him to see what he was doing. So then I found the name James Brown was forming a small band and he needed a drummer. Well in the meantime also, Mr. Thompson, our barber, he had been in the Cavalry I think back in the Midwest. And he’d been in the Cavalry band. So in his basement he had all these instruments and all this music. So he put together a small teenage band. And I played drums in the band. He got me in there, of course I couldn’t read any music. So then when James Brown, the bass player, he had been a student of Vern Alley’s, he formed a band and needed a drummer. So they recommended me. So I had to join the union.

Yeah. I’m seventeen. So what happened, our business agent then, see we were a subsidiary local. Our business agent lived in the area so they gave him my — they told him how to get in touch with me and he came by my house one day and said, “I understand you wanted to join the union?” “Yeah.” So I said, “Well I don’t have any money.” He said, “Well how much do you have?” I said, “Well I’ve got five dollars.” He said, “Give me the five dollars.” So five dollars down, and every time I’d see him on the street if I had a couple of dollars in my pocket — so one day finally he said, “Okay, here’s your ticket.”
And there was no like musical audition for that?
Okay. It was kind of like by recommendation that they would let you in.
